title: Improving the Consistency in Cross-Lingual Cross-Modal Retrieval with 1-to-K Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Cross-lingual cross-modal retrieval must support image-text retrieval across multiple languages and modalities with a single model.

gap.claim: Existing approaches exhibit inconsistency from intra-modal error propagation across languages and inter-modal optimization-direction bias within instances.

contributions.claim: A 1-to-K contrastive learning method treats languages equally and is intended to eliminate error propagation and optimization bias.
Mean Rank Variance (MRV) measures rank inconsistency across languages within each instance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four CCR datasets report improved recall rates and MRV with smaller-scale pre-trained data.
The authors report achieving the new state-of-the-art.

narrative_sequence.summary: CCR addresses multilingual image-text retrieval with a single model.
Cross-lingual cross-modal pre-training and contrastive learning have improved retrieval.
Existing methods produce cross-language inconsistency through error propagation and optimization bias.
The paper proposes 1-to-K contrastive learning and MRV, then reports experiments across four datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract identifies inconsistency across languages as distinct from aggregate retrieval performance.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation may need metrics that expose cross-language consistency rather than relying only on Recall@K.

application.claim: For multilingual retrieval systems, pair aggregate recall with a within-instance cross-language rank-consistency metric.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether MRV generalizes beyond the reported CCR datasets or settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, implementation details, or numerical effect sizes.
The abstract does not provide the formal definition of MRV or the 1-to-K objective.
